security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives in documentation examples, checklists, and Markdown resource references. The only confirmed issue is a FastAPI template that binds uvicorn to all interfaces. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The FastAPI template binds uvicorn to 0.0.0.0 by default.
remediation.suggestion: Default the template to 127.0.0.1 and document when all-interface binding is appropriate.

content.user_title: Design Better REST and GraphQL APIs
content.value_statement: API teams need consistent contracts that are easy to use and maintain. This skill guides REST and GraphQL design with templates, checklists, and review criteria.
actual_capabilities: Guides REST resource naming, HTTP methods, status codes, and pagination choices.
Explains GraphQL schema structure, connections, mutations, subscriptions, and custom scalars.
Provides API review checklists for contracts, errors, versioning, security, and documentation.
Includes a FastAPI sample template for resource models and endpoint structure.
Covers DataLoader patterns and query-depth controls for GraphQL performance.
limitations: Does not replace security testing, load testing, or production architecture review.
Does not generate a complete application for a specific framework without adaptation.
Requires project context to choose the right API style and versioning strategy.
Example code and placeholder domains must be reviewed before production use.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Public API
use_cases.description: Define resources, schemas, errors, pagination, and versioning before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Contract
use_cases.description: Check REST or GraphQL designs for consistency, usability, security posture, and documentation gaps.

use_cases.title: Create Team Standards
use_cases.description: Turn design guidance into reusable API rules, review checklists, and onboarding material.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an API Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose REST or GraphQL for this service. Consumers: [list]. Core use cases: [list]. Constraints: [latency, clients, auth, team skills].

prompt_templates.title: Draft REST Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design REST resources for [domain]. Include resource names, methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, error format, and versioning guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review a GraphQL Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this GraphQL schema for naming, nullability, pagination, mutation payloads, errors, authorization boundaries, and N+1 risks: [schema summary].

prompt_templates.title: Create an API Governance Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a practical API design checklist for our team. Cover REST, GraphQL, auth, errors, docs, observability, versioning, and review gates.

output_examples.input: A team needs a user management REST API design review.
output: Resource naming recommendations for users, roles, and invitations.
Status code guidance for create, update, delete, and validation failures.
Pagination, filtering, error response, and versioning review notes.

output_examples.input: A product team needs a GraphQL schema for orders and customers.
output: Mutation payload guidance with structured errors.
Performance notes for batching, query depth, and resolver boundaries.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants reusable API standards.
output: A concise review checklist for design proposals.
Rules for naming, pagination, authentication, errors, and documentation.
Common anti-patterns to block during contract review.

best_practices: Start with consumers, use cases, and constraints before choosing REST or GraphQL.
Keep API contracts consistent across naming, errors, pagination, authentication, and versioning.
Validate designs with examples, review checklists, and implementation constraints before release.
anti_patterns: Choosing GraphQL or REST based only on preference instead of consumer needs.
Shipping inconsistent error formats, status codes, or pagination behavior across endpoints.
Copying sample templates into production without security and environment review.

faq.question: Does this skill support both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes REST best practices and GraphQL schema design guidance.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready API code?
faq.answer: No. It includes examples and templates that require project-specific review and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers developer-friendly documentation, examples, and OpenAPI-oriented review practices.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It can surface design concerns, but security testing and expert review remain necessary.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Backend engineers, technical leads, platform teams, and API reviewers can use it.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from REST to GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps compare styles and plan contracts, but migration details need system context.
